title: COP31 Talks in Antalya Stall Over Fossil Fuels as Week One Closes
dek: Negotiators end the first week divided over fossil-fuel language and climate finance, while host Turkey pushes an electrification pledge that has drawn few public endorsements.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Wide view of a COP31 Presidency energy ministerial meeting
image.credit: Necati Savas / European Union (EC Audiovisual Service)

keyPoints: The UN says COP31 runs from Nov. 9 to Nov. 20 in Antalya, Türkiye, under a joint Turkish-Australian presidency.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for an 'immediate and drastic reduction' in emissions as fossil-fuel divisions dominated the first week, Reuters reported.
Big fossil-fuel producers and consumers are resisting firm new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal, Reuters reported.

Turkey wants a pledge that 35% of global final energy comes from electricity by 2035; Carbon Brief understands more than 50 countries are firm signatories or supporters, though few have said so publicly.
A draft cover decision is due early next week, Carbon Brief reported, while the climate finance work programme remains stalled.
body:
## Week one ends without a fossil-fuel deal

The first week of COP31 ended with the hardest questions unresolved. Reuters reported on Friday that major oil producers and large consumers were resisting any text that would set firm new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal. Saudi Arabia and Russia have traditionally resisted language that constrains fossil fuels, and India has opposed measures it says could limit development, Reuters reported, a dynamic that has compromised past outcomes.

Guterres said in remarks reported by Reuters: "The central question is in the hands of member states, particularly the big emitters." He called for an immediate and drastic cut in emissions to keep the 1.5C goal possible. A UN report published last month found the world is on course to exceed 1.5C. Guterres is leaving his post at the end of December after two five-year terms.

## Procedure and the cover decision

Carbon Brief reported that talks got off to a smoother start than many expected after avoiding a fight over the agenda. Draft texts have emerged from most negotiating tracks, but the most contentious issue, a new climate finance work programme, remains stalled. The presidency's push for an overarching "cover decision" has faced procedural pushback from Russia and others, Carbon Brief reported, and a draft is due early next week.

The Earth Negotiations Bulletin's daily report for Nov. 13 describes presidency consultations on the cover decision, where the co-facilitators invited views on an informal note.

## Electrification as the host's flagship

Turkey and Australia are pushing a pledge that 35% of global final energy come from electricity by 2035. Reuters reported that the proposal does not require the extra electricity to come from renewable sources, while some countries, including Brazil, want progress on a plan requiring governments to map out their transition away from fossil fuels. NPR, citing Ember analyst Kingsmill Bond, put the current electrification rate at about 23%.

Carbon Brief reported the pledge has drawn few public endorsements so far, though more than 50 countries are understood to be firm signatories or supporters, and many others remain undecided.

## The backdrop

The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, now in its ninth month, has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and pushed oil and gas prices higher, NPR reported. That has sharpened the energy-security case for electrification, which supporters argue makes solar, batteries and electric vehicles easier to back. The United States skipped the talks for a second year in a row, Reuters reported.

## What to watch

The coming week will show whether the cover decision, fossil-fuel language and the finance work programme advance. The Brazilian COP30 presidency formally presented its global fossil-fuel roadmap at a plenary attended by Guterres, Carbon Brief reported. Nothing has been agreed. The next checkpoints are the draft cover decision early next week and the close of talks on Nov. 20.
